lacks.null-list: The harness stores aNumberList as adversarial_number_list rows, one per element, so a null list and [] are both zero rows: a row sent to the PDP as null cannot be stored.

arithmetic/add/ternary-selecting-double-.reason: Same int() refusal as arithmetic/divide/int-truncates: SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL's int() conversion, so the addition over the ternary is never reached.

arithmetic/divide/field-by-field.reason: Cannot translate a division by a floating-point column or by computed arithmetic: its zero may be -0.0, which CEL divides a non-zero number into the opposite infinity from 0.0, while SQL compares -0.0 equal to 0.0 and has no portable way to read the sign bit. Divide by an integer or decimal column, or by a constant.

arithmetic/divide/int-truncates.reason: Cannot translate int(): SQL CAST reads the numeric prefix of a string where CEL requires the whole string and raises otherwise, and PostgreSQL and MySQL round where CEL truncates toward zero, so the cast would admit rows the PDP denies.

arithmetic/divide/nested-division-diviso.reason: A division as the DIVISOR: the inner division can be a zero-denominator NaN or infinity, SQL has no literal for either, and against a column the sign of the result depends on that column. arithmetic/modulo/column-divisor-negativ.reason: mod is not supported in comparisons: CEL % is integer-only while attribute values are always doubles at check time, so a satisfiable policy must cast with int() first — and int() has no faithful SQL lowering, because CAST rounds where CEL truncates toward zero.

arithmetic/modulo/negative-dividend.reason: CEL `%` is integer-only while an attribute value is always a double at check time, so a satisfiable policy has to cast with int() first, and int() has no faithful SQL lowering: CAST rounds to nearest on PostgreSQL and MySQL where CEL truncates toward zero. The modulo is refused by name before its operands are read, on the same ground that refuses `cast/int/negative-fraction`

arithmetic/multiply/nan-times-zero-plus-.reason: arithmetic between a column and the NaN or infinity a zero denominator produces is not supported: SQL has no literal for either value, and neither folds to one constant against a column, because an infinity times or divided by a column depends on that column's sign. Compare the division itself, or keep the composition constant.

collection/intersect/duplicates-in-short.reason: Cerbos's intersect() keeps duplicates from whichever list is shorter, so size(intersect(a, b)) depends on the two lists' lengths, which no SQL set operation or correlated count reproduces. intersect() is translated only compared with an empty list, where it is hasIntersection()

collection/map/as-whole-condition.reason: map() returns a list, not a boolean, so it cannot be a condition on its own; only hasIntersection(map(...), [...]) gives the list a scalar meaning

collection/map/equals-list-literal.reason: map() is held as a deferred projection until hasIntersection() gives it a scalar meaning, as the inner select of an EXISTS; that is the only consumer this adapter has for one, and size(map(...)) is refused as well. Comparing the ORDERED projection itself to a literal list gives it no scalar meaning, and a correlated subquery cannot be compared to a list value

comparison/equals/list-holding-nan.reason: Cannot compare a column with a list() value: a mapped column holds one scalar, which SQL equality cannot compare with a list.

comparison/equals/whole-list-literal.reason: Whole-list equality against a relation. tagNames is a related table, and a correlated subquery cannot be compared with a list value as one ordered whole

comparison/equals/whole-list-literal-ord.reason: Whole-list equality against a relation. tagNames is a related table, and a correlated subquery cannot be compared with a list value as one ordered whole, so neither the order nor the multiplicity CEL compares can be expressed

comparison/not-equals/whole-list-literal.reason: Whole-list inequality against a relation. tagNames is a related table, and a correlated subquery cannot be compared with a list value as one ordered whole

The translator walks both branches, so the refusal comes even where the condition never takes that branch.

conditional/ternary/string-match-receive.reason: A ternary is distributed into its branches only as an operand of ==, !=, <, <=, > or >=; as the receiver of contains() it is refused.

hierarchy/overlaps/field-to-field.reason: Both hierarchies are read from columns, so there is no constant path to expand into prefixes, and an Exposed expression cannot split a column on a delimiter to compare it segment by segment.

logic/and/non-boolean-operand-in-value-n.reason: An and() whose result is compared with `==` as a value has no translation: the walker lowers and() only in condition position, and refuses it as an operand of eq.

regex/matches/anchored-prefix-dot-star.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; a .* not followed by an end anchor is refused.

regex/matches/case-insensitive-non-ascii.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; (?i) is spelled as ASCII case alternatives, so a non-ASCII letter under it is refused.

regex/matches/dot-all-flag.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; an inline flag other than a leading (?i) is refused.

regex/matches/end-anchor-mid-pattern.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; an anchor followed by more pattern is refused.

regex/matches/field-to-field.reason: matches() is compiled into LIKE at translation, so it is translated only against a constant pattern; a pattern read from a row is refused.

regex/matches/negated-class.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; a negated character class has no LIKE spelling and is refused.

regex/matches/non-digit-class.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; \D has no LIKE spelling and is refused.

regex/matches/unanchored-dot.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; a lone . would become _, which matches a newline RE2's . does not, so it is refused.

regex/matches/unanchored-quantifiers.reason: matches() is translated only where LIKE, = and REPLACE spell the RE2 pattern exactly: finite alternatives, anchored .* and .+, and ^[set]*$. An unbounded repetition of a literal (x*, a+) inside a pattern has no finite expansion and no LIKE wildcard that counts only one character's repeats, so it is refused when the pattern is compiled

regex/matches/unbounded-count.reason: matches() is translated only where LIKE, = and REPLACE spell the RE2 pattern exactly; the unbounded run `.{8,}` is lowered only as `.*` or `.+` between finite parts, so it is refused when the pattern is compiled

regex/matches/word-boundary.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; \b has no LIKE spelling and is refused.

size/greater-than/map-projection.reason: size() takes a mapped collection or a filter(); a map() projection is refused, since its body is evaluated per element and one erroring element (b6's unnamed tag) makes the count an error.

string/concatenate/negated-null-principa.reason: A null principal attribute reaches the plan as a null constant beside add; CEL has no overload for it and the adapter does not model the error, so it refuses rather than fold the concatenation.

timestamp/equals/field-to-field-without-.reason: Two instant columns compared WITHOUT timestamp(): CEL compares their RFC 3339 STRINGS, so one instant written two ways is unequal, while SQL compares instants. The operand-type guard refuses two temporal columns under a plain comparison

type-mismatch/equals/number-list-element.reason: Positional access into a list. Every list this adapter reads is a related table behind a correlated subquery, and the rows it returns carry no CEL list order for a position to index into. Refused in the leaf operand, by the operator's own name

type-mismatch/less-than/negated-nan-agai.reason: CEL compares values of different types without coercion — equality is a definite false and ordering a no-overload error — while SQL coerces one side (MySQL coerces the string column to a number). The operand-type guard compares the constant's or the other column's type with the mapped column's declared type and refuses a mismatch before any SQL is built
